extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets and American writers (readers/producers of lyric/poetic work)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and aesthetic guidance for poets (especially American) on what makes great poetry: values, style, subject, and craft—emphasizing simplicity, individuality, democratic inclusiveness, and engagement with science and the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of classical and mythic models
rubrics_metrics.description: These, I say, are models... (lists Yudishtura, Rama, Arjuna, Solomon, Achilles, Ulysses, Theseus, Prometheus, Hercules, Aeneas, Merlin, Cid, Arthur, Siegfried, Hagen, Roland, Oliver, Roustam, Milton's Satan, Cervantes' Don Quixote, Shakespeare's Hamlet, Richard II., Lear, Marc Antony, &c.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat standard heroic/mythic figures as invaluable models and studies; combine and adjust them to national standards. Use them as study-materials to enrich new work rather than simply imitating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: American poetic voice: enclose old and new; be transcendent and new
rubrics_metrics.description: The American poets are to enclose old and new, for America is the race of races. The expression of the American poet is to be transcendent and new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend inherited traditions with new, original perspectives. Avoid mere imitation of foreign modes; create a voice that is both rooted and innovating—transcendent more than merely descriptive or epic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirectness over literal description
rubrics_metrics.description: It is to be indirect, and not direct or descriptive or epic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor suggestive, oblique, or visionary approaches rather than plain descriptive narration or epic recitation. Let implication and resonance carry meaning rather than straightforward reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity as the supreme artistic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of art, the glory of expression and the sunshine of the light of letters, is simplicity. Nothing is better than simplicity—nothing can make up for excess, or for the lack of definiteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune excess, aim for definiteness and clarity. Simplicity should govern diction, structure, and gesture; a simple mode often accomplishes the deepest artistic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural, unconstraint style; writing like animal movement
rubrics_metrics.description: To speak in literature with the perfect rectitude and insouciance of the movements of animals, and the unimpeachableness of the sentiment of trees in the woods and grass by the roadside, is the flawless triumph of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for a spontaneous, unforced voice—movements and phrases should feel inevitable and natural. Avoid affected or labored phrasing; write as if the lines moved effortlessly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ornamental effects that obstruct communication
rubrics_metrics.description: I will not be meddlesome, I will not have in my writing any elegance, or effect, or originality, to hang in the way between me and the rest like curtains. I will have nothing hang in the way, not the richest curtains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let ornament, flashy originality, or clever effects stand between the reader and the poem's core. Transparency of utterance is preferable to conspicuous stylistic displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's ethical life shapes poetry (moral comportment and habits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Love the earth and sun and the animals, despise riches, give alms to every one that asks, stand up for the stupid and crazy, devote your income and labor to others, hate tyrants, argue not concerning God, have patience and indulgence toward the people...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate humility, generosity, and affection in life—these dispositions are essential sources of poetic material and tone. The poem's life comes from the poet's lived ethics and close relation to common humanity and nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as seer and individual
rubrics_metrics.description: He is a seer—he is individual—he is complete in himself—the others are as good as he, only he sees it, and they do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value distinct vision and inner completeness. A great poet perceives beyond ordinary sight and expresses a self-contained perspective that others may not yet recognize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remould rather than merely attack; prove artistic worth by creation
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to destroy or remould is freely used by the greatest poet, but seldom the power of attack. What is past is past. If he does not expose superior models, and prove himself by every step he takes, he is not what is wanted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than polemicizing or scorning earlier works, transform and renew tradition through constructive creation. Let your work demonstrate superiority by embodying fresh solutions, not by denunciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect temporalities; revive the past and make future present
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest poet forms the consistence of what is to be, from what has been and is. He drags the dead out of their coffins and stands them again on their feet. He says to the past, Rise and walk before me that I may realize you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make poems that synthesize past, present, and future—use past materials to energize contemporary meaning and to suggest unfolding continuities rather than static antiquarianism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid didactic moralizing; dwell in the soul rather than preach
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest poet does not moralize or make applications of morals—he knows the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer inward, sympathetic revelation over overt moral lessons. Let the poem disclose character and inner truth rather than instruct explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic accessibility and equality of audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The messages of great poems to each man and woman are, Come to us on equal terms, only then can you understand us. We are no better than you, what we inclose you inclose, what we enjoy you may enjoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write poems that invite and include broad readerships; avoid elitism or exclusivity. Great poetry addresses people on equal footing and affirms shared human capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generosity among poets; encourage competitors; eschew privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: The American bards shall be mark'd for generosity and affection, and for encouraging competitors. They shall not be careful of riches and privilege—they shall be riches and privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster a poetic community of mutual encouragement rather than secrecy or hoarding. Treat other poets as equals and welcome competition as enrichment rather than threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use science and other disciplines as sources and supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Exact science and its practical movements are no checks on the greatest poet, but always his encouragement and support... the anatomist, chemist, astronomer, geologist, phrenologist, spiritualist, mathematician, historian, and lexicographer, are not poets, but they are the lawgivers of poets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw upon scientific knowledge and varied fields for images, structure, and validation. Interdisciplinary reference enriches poetic conception and grounds imagination in demonstrable fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create original practical examples and new forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the traits ... he is greatest for ever and ever who contributes the greatest original practical example. The cleanest expression is that which finds no sphere worthy of itself, and makes one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When existing forms are inadequate, invent new genres or modes. Demonstrable, practical originality—examples that others can follow—is a chief virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and suggestiveness: let faint indications suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose must surely be there, and the clue of it must be there—and the faintest indication is the indication of the best, and then becomes the clearest indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust suggestion and economy: a subtle hint can be more powerful than expansive exposition. Ensure the poem contains a clear purpose or clue, even when expressed minimally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go directly to creation; avoid unneeded busywork
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet shall not spend his time in unneeded work. He shall know that the ground is already plough'd and manured; others may not know it, but he shall. He shall go directly to the creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus effort on the essential act of making rather than on redundant preparatory labor. Recognize cultural groundwork but proceed confidently to produce original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over mere technical virtuosity
rubrics_metrics.description: The best singer is not the one who has the most lithe and powerful organ. The pleasure of poems is not in them that take the handsomest measure and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize technical display (perfect meter, vocal prowess) above emotional / visionary substance. Formal mastery should serve expressive truth, not replace it.
